signals.topic: Sandbox LocalDir copy follows symlink-swapped sources, allowing arbitrary file write into sandbox workspace
signals.summary: When a LocalDir source path is validated as a real directory and then atomically swapped to a symlink before or during the copy operation, the SDK's copy implementation follows the swapped symlink target and writes files from it into the sandbox workspace. This allows a path-confined operation to escape its boundary and overwrite arbitrary files inside the sandbox.
aliases: sandbox path traversal via symlink race
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed security bug with a reproducible PoC: a LocalDir validated as a real directory can be atomically swapped to a symlink, causing the SDK's copy operation to write arbitrary files into the sandbox workspace. This is not a theoretical concern — the reporter demonstrates NO_RAISE on current main for both relative and root-relative source paths, meaning the sandbox's isolation guarantee is broken. The fix (PR #3408) exists and confirms the severity.

source_issues.title: Sandbox LocalDir copy can follow symlink-swapped sources
source_issues.evidence: Reproduced on openai-agents-python@65774ce8: LocalDir(src=Path('src')) and LocalDir(src=Path('.')) both wrote /workspace/copied/secret.txt when source was swapped to symlink; NO_RAISE — no exception raised. Fix branch (97b5c193) adds pre-open no-follow stat checks and post-open identity comparisons.

signals.topic: Realtime tool call exceptions leave model hanging indefinitely — no tool output sent, session appears unresponsive
signals.summary: In the Realtime session's known-tool branch, when a tool raises an exception (e.g., timeout, ValueError), the exception propagates and is logged, but no RealtimeModelSendToolOutput is sent back to the model. The model waits for a function call result that never arrives until the server-side timeout fires (~30 seconds), during which the session appears to hang.
aliases: known tool exception no model output
Realtime session hangs after tool exception
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed runtime bug that causes a 30-second session hang in Realtime agent sessions. When any known tool raises an exception (timeout, user error, or any runtime failure), the model receives no output and waits indefinitely — the session is completely unresponsive until the server-side timeout fires. The bug is reproducible with a self-contained script and the fix path is clear (mirror the #3287 pattern for the known-tool exception branch). This directly blocks production Realtime workflows.

source_issues.title: Realtime known tool failures (exception/timeout) do not send model-visible output
source_issues.evidence: Repro script demonstrates: ValueError raised, Model received tool output: False, Local error emitted but no tool output sent to model. Compare: unknown-tool branch (fixed by #3287) correctly sends RealtimeModelSendToolOutput with error message. Known-tool success path sends start_response=True. Only the known-tool exception branch is broken. Existing test at test_session.py:1199 codifies the missing behavior as expected.

signals.topic: Unknown/hallucinated tool names abort entire agent run with no recovery path
signals.summary: When the model returns a function tool call for a tool name not registered in the current agent (model hallucination, dynamic tool loading, or tool availability changes), the SDK raises ModelBehaviorError and aborts the entire run. In long-running agent sessions, there is no recovery mechanism — the full workflow is lost.
signals.review_reason: This bug causes the entire agent run to abort when the model calls a tool that is not registered, which can happen due to model hallucination, dynamic tool registration, or changing tool availability. The abort is unrecoverable — the full agent run state is lost. This is particularly painful in long-running multi-turn workflows where the agent has already completed significant work before the hallucinated tool call. The feature:core label and enhancement classification confirm the team acknowledges this as a real gap.

source_issues.title: Make unknown tool calls recoverable instead of aborting with ModelBehaviorError
source_issues.evidence: Path: process_model_response() -> build_function_tool_lookup_map() -> function_map.get(...) is None -> raise ModelBehaviorError. Triggered by model tool name hallucination, dynamic tool loading, or tool availability changes between turns. In long-running agent sessions, aborting the entire run is difficult to recover from.

signals.topic: Structured output parsing raises Pydantic ValidationError instead of surfacing incomplete response status
signals.summary: When using Responses API with structured output (Pydantic text_format), the SDK parses JSON before checking the terminal response status. If the API returns an incomplete response (e.g., truncated by max_output_tokens), the parser raises a Pydantic ValidationError ('EOF while parsing object') instead of surfacing the incomplete status. This masks the real error cause and prevents callers from handling incomplete responses gracefully. Affects both streaming (response.output_text.done event) and non-streaming (parse_response) paths.
aliases: streaming structured output incomplete JSON error
signals.review_reason: Two independent reports (streaming path #3263, non-streaming path #2486) confirm the same root cause: structured output parsing happens before checking response status. When a response is incomplete (e.g., truncated by max_output_tokens), users get a confusing Pydantic JSON validation error instead of a clear incomplete status. This prevents proper error handling in production applications using structured outputs.

source_issues.title: Responses streaming structured output parses incomplete JSON before terminal incomplete status
source_issues.evidence: Streaming: SDK parses JSON on response.output_text.done event before terminal status is known. When API emits response.incomplete (e.g., truncated by max_output_tokens), Pydantic raises 'EOF while parsing object'. Application code cannot handle incomplete status before the parse error.

source_issues.title: Incomplete responses are not handled by parse_response when using Structured Output
source_issues.evidence: Non-streaming: parse_response calls parse_text() on incomplete message text, raising Pydantic ValidationError. Full stack trace provided. Affects anyone using structured output with max_output_tokens that can truncate. Open since July 2025.

signals.topic: v2.34.0 auth refactor breaks existing Azure AD bearer-token-via-api_key workflow with 401
signals.summary: In 2.34.0 the auth credential handling was refactored: api_key is now sent as an `api-key` header instead of `Authorization: Bearer`, causing Azure AD bearer tokens passed via api_key to return 401 and breaking the upgrade path for Azure deployments behind API Management proxies.
aliases: Azure AD bearer token via api_key broken in 2.34.0
signals.review_reason: Confirmed breaking change from an upgrade: v2.34.0 silently changed how api_key is sent (Bearer vs api-key header), causing 401 for users who pass Azure AD bearer tokens via api_key. This blocks the Azure deployment workflow for users behind API Management proxies who relied on the prior auth behavior.

source_issues.title: AzureOpenAI with AAD bearer token passed via api_key works in 2.33.0 but returns 401 in 2.34.0 and after
source_issues.evidence: Same code works in 2.33.0, fails with 401 'Access denied' in 2.34.0+. Root cause is api_key now sent as api-key header instead of Bearer token. Affects Azure deployments with custom base_url/APIM proxies.

signals.topic: Non-streaming API calls hang indefinitely behind NAT due to missing TCP keepalive in default httpx transport
signals.summary: The default httpx transport used by the SDK has no TCP keepalive enabled. On deployments behind NAT gateways (AWS NAT, GCP Cloud NAT, home routers), idle TCP connections are silently dropped after 60–350s. With long-running reasoning models (300–700s generation time), the connection is dropped mid-generation, and the client hangs forever without error — the response is never received despite being generated server-side.
aliases: long reasoning calls hang in production
signals.review_reason: Main flow blocking: non-streaming calls hang forever in production. Root cause is clearly identified (no TCP keepalive), widely affects cloud deployments behind NAT (EKS, ECS, Cloud Run, GKE), and is reproducible with long-running reasoning models. OpenAI dashboard confirms server-side completion while client blocks indefinitely. This is a high-severity silent failure that causes production request hangs.

source_issues.title: [Bug] Non-streaming calls silently hang forever behind NAT — default httpx transport has no TCP keepalive
source_issues.evidence: Reproducer confirms: with gpt-5.4+high reasoning (~606s), OpenAI dashboard shows completion but client hangs forever. Adding TCP keepalive fixes it. PR #3270 submitted. Affects all cloud deployments (EKS, ECS, Cloud Run, GKE) behind NAT — widespread production impact.

signals.topic: v2.34.0 credential validation rejects empty api_key, breaking OpenAI-compatible local servers
signals.summary: In 2.34.0, passing api_key="" to AsyncOpenAI/OpenAI now raises OpenAIError: Missing credentials. In v2.33.0 and earlier this was silently accepted. This breaks all workflows using the SDK to talk to local servers (llama.cpp, llamafile, LM Studio, vLLM) that intentionally pass an empty api_key because no authentication is required.
signals.review_reason: Confirmed breaking change from upgrade that blocks a legitimate use case: connecting to local LLM servers that require no authentication. The new credential validation in 2.34.0 is too strict and rejects a pattern that worked in all prior versions. Widespread impact for local development and open-source LLM users.

source_issues.title: AsyncOpenAI(api_key="") raises OpenAIError in v2.34.0, breaking OpenAI-compatible local servers
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed breaking change across Python 3.11, 3.12, 3.13 on Linux/macOS. All local LLM server users (llama.cpp, llamafile, LM Studio, vLLM) are affected. Workaround is non-obvious (pass 'not-needed' placeholder).

signals.topic: Streaming SSE parser crashes with JSONDecodeError on valid meta-only events (retry, id, event fields with no data)
signals.summary: The streaming implementation throws JSONDecodeError when SSE events contain only meta-fields (retry, id, event) with no data field. Per the WHATWG SSE specification, meta-only events are valid. The parser calls .json() on all events including those with empty data, causing a crash instead of gracefully skipping them.
signals.review_reason: Streaming flow crashes with JSONDecodeError on valid SSE meta-only events (e.g., retry directives from proxies/gateways). This is a well-documented bug per the WHATWG SSE spec — meta-only events are valid, but the SDK doesn't handle them. Causes streaming to fail entirely for affected deployments.

source_issues.title: Streaming: JSONDecodeError when SSE events contain only meta-fields (retry, id, event)
source_issues.evidence: Crash confirmed: JSONDecodeError at openai/_streaming.py line 82 calling sse.json() on empty data. Root cause is missing guard for empty/missing data field in SSE events. Fix in PR #2721. Affects users behind proxies/gateways that add SSE retry directives.

signals.topic: Skill incorrectly flagged as malicious — false positive security autoban blocking legitimate tools
signals.summary: Multiple legitimate skills have been incorrectly flagged as malicious by ClawHub's automated security scanner, resulting in skills being hidden from browse/search, labeled as 'malicious' on the registry, and their publishers' accounts entering autoban states. At least two separate skills (agentauth and markdown2doc) have been caught in this pattern, requiring repeated manual appeals with no automated resolution.
signals.review_reason: 关键功能不可用：被错误标记的技能从公开 registry 隐藏，publisher 账号进入 autoban 状态，核心发布和发现流程被阻断。count=2 有明确去重证据（两个不同 skill 的独立报告），impact:security 标签支撑。

source_issues.title: [Skill Appeal] markdown2doc incorrectly flagged as malicious
source_issues.evidence: Third appeal for same skill; moderator confirmed fix in prior ticket but malicious label still present on live platform; publisher's account was in malware-autoban state; audit report explicitly contradicted the label; publisher cannot get resolution despite repeated engagement

source_issues.title: False positive: agentauth flagged as suspicious — FIDO2 consent gate
source_issues.evidence: Legitimate FIDO2/WebAuthn passkey consent gate incorrectly flagged as suspicious; core security functionality (human approval before dangerous operations) was misidentified as malicious pattern; skill resolved after manual review and rescan

signals.topic: Skill publish fails with embedding token limit error despite small SKILL.md
signals.summary: Users attempting to publish skills encounter a '8192 token' embedding error even when their SKILL.md files are well under that size. The embedding pipeline silently truncates content before sending to the model, causing publishing to fail completely. A linked fix PR exists.
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：用户无法发布任何技能（核心发布流程完全失败），有复现步骤和 linked PR，issue-rating 为 diamond lobster（最高严重等级）。虽然仅单仓单 issue，但有明确的主流程阻断证据支撑 P0 定级。

source_issues.title: [Bug] Skill publish fails with "8192 token" embedding error despite small SKILL.md
source_issues.evidence: Users cannot publish skills; embedding pipeline truncates content causing 8192-token failures despite small source files; linked fix PR open

signals.topic: clawhub install does not register OpenClaw skill hooks — silent failure
signals.summary: When installing skills that include OpenClaw hooks (hooks/openclaw/HOOK.md), the clawhub install command copies files to the workspace but never registers the hook with the gateway. The skill appears 'installed' in the UI but the hook never fires. Users have no warning that an extra manual step is required. After clawhub install, users must manually run openclaw plugins install and restart the gateway for hooks to work.
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断（静默）：安装命令表面成功但核心功能（hook）完全不可用，用户无感知需要额外手动步骤。属于关键功能不可用的静默失败，issue-rating 为 diamond lobster，影响 OpenClaw hook 机制的核心能力。

source_issues.title: clawhub install does not register skill hooks automatically
source_issues.evidence: Skill installs appear successful in UI/CLI but hooks silently do nothing; user has no indication extra manual steps are needed; confirmed with self-improving-agent skill on OpenClaw 2026.5.12; workaround requires manual plugin install + gateway restart

signals.topic: Account recovery blocked after self-deleted ClawHub account — GitHub identity cannot be reused
signals.summary: Users who delete their ClawHub account get stuck unable to use the same GitHub identity again. While GitHub OAuth authorization succeeds at the provider level, ClawHub rejects or loops because the old ClawHub user record, deleted-account marker, and provider identity binding remain reserved. This issue consolidates 16 prior duplicate reports over an extended period, indicating a persistent, high-impact blocker for account recovery workflows.
signals.review_reason: 会话状态阻断：虽然当前有 workaround（手动 admin 操作），但 16 次重复报告证明这是高频长期待解决的真实用户痛点，导致已删除账户用户永久无法用相同 GitHub 身份重新注册。impact:auth-provider 和 P1 标签均为维护者自评，keep=true。

source_issues.title: Account recovery: allow fresh signup after self-deleted account purge
source_issues.evidence: Issue explicitly consolidates 16 prior duplicate reports (#32, #504, #886, #900, #907, #917, #1046, #1116, #1244, #1267, #1282, #1452, #1620, #1900, #2025, #2181); blocked users cannot sign up with same GitHub identity after account deletion; OAuth succeeds at provider but ClawHub rejects the flow

signals.topic: Skill download counts frozen — publisher metrics stale since May 18
signals.summary: All skill download counts on ClawHub have stopped incrementing since May 18, 2026. New versions have been published (v2.0.0 → v2.0.1 → v2.0.2) but download numbers remain unchanged across all affected publishers' skills. This breaks publisher adoption tracking and search ranking signals that depend on download counts.
signals.review_reason: 明显成本损失：download count 是生态平台的核心指标，直接影响技能发现排序和 publisher 决策。多个技能计数同时冻结具有明显性，虽然非主流程阻断但属于关键数据不可用。impact:data-loss 标签支撑。

source_issues.title: Skill download counts frozen since May 18
source_issues.evidence: Download counter pipeline stopped on May 18; multiple skills across publisher z-zihan all show frozen counts; affects version updates and user installs; explicitly flags whether download counter pipeline is still running

signals.topic: Uninstall leaves behind empty directories in %LOCALAPPDATA%
signals.summary: After full uninstall (WSL uninstall + MSIX uninstall), empty `wsl\` and `OpenClawTray\` directories remain on disk. Root cause: Step 7 of LocalGatewayUninstall.cs deletes VHD subdirectory but not parent `wsl\` directory.
signals.review_reason: This is a genuine user pain point: uninstall leaves persistent empty directories on disk after complete removal flow, indicating incomplete cleanup. While count=1, the issue has clear repro steps, confirmed root cause, and a suggested fix — it is a real post-uninstall residual artifact problem that users can observe on their machines.

source_issues.title: Uninstall leaves behind empty directories in %LOCALAPPDATA%
source_issues.evidence: Repro: install MSIX, run easy-button setup, remove local gateway via tray, uninstall MSIX. Empty %LOCALAPPDATA%\OpenClawTray\wsl\ and %LOCALAPPDATA%\OpenClawTray\ remain. Root cause identified in LocalGatewayUninstall.cs Step 7.

signals.topic: Toggling 'Allow screen recording' in Settings briefly hides left-nav items (UI strobe)
signals.summary: When toggling the screen recording consent setting in Settings, the left navigation temporarily collapses gateway-gated items (Chat, Sessions, Skills, Channels, Instances, Advanced) for the duration of a reconnect blip, creating a visible UI strobe effect.
aliases: nav visibility strobe on settings toggle
signals.review_reason: This is a real UX degradation: toggling an unrelated setting causes the entire left navigation to strobe and temporarily collapse. While intermittent, it is user-observable during a settings interaction. Root cause is identified (UpdateGatewayNavVisibility fires on every non-Connected state). This is not a main-flow blocker but it is a clear experience degradation during a common interaction path.

source_issues.title: [msix-e2e-feedback] Toggling 'Allow screen recording' in Settings briefly hides left-nav items
source_issues.evidence: Repro: toggle 'Allow screen recording' ON in Settings. Left nav items (Chat/Sessions/Skills/Channels/Instances/Advanced) briefly disappear. Root cause: HubWindow.UpdateGatewayNavVisibility collapses nav on any non-Connected state; settings toggle causes a brief gateway disconnect. Intermittent because nav restores before user notices. Found during MSIX-E2E manual test pass.

signals.topic: WinUI tray app: trackpad two-finger scroll doesn't work on some devboxes
signals.summary: On some cloud devboxes, the WinUI tray app does not respond to trackpad two-finger scroll gestures in scrollable surfaces (Settings, Chat, etc.). Mouse wheel works fine. Browser scroll on the same machine works fine, indicating a WinUI-specific input configuration issue.
aliases: trackpad scroll broken in WinUI tray
two-finger scroll not working on cloud devboxes
signals.review_reason: This is a genuine user pain point: trackpad scrolling is broken for WinUI tray app on some dev environments, making navigation in Settings and Chat unusable without a mouse. While observed on cloud devboxes specifically, the same configuration gap would affect any user with this hardware/environment combination. This blocks a primary input method for scrolling.

source_issues.title: [msix-e2e-feedback] WinUI: trackpad two-finger scroll doesn't work in tray app on some devboxes
source_issues.evidence: Repro: install msix-e2e-test-build on a cloud devbox, open scrollable surface, try two-finger scroll. No effect. Mouse wheel works. Browser scroll on same machine works. Works on local devbox. Found during MSIX-E2E manual test pass. Suggests missing precision-touchpad input mode opt-in in WinUI ScrollViewer configuration.

signals.topic: Chat attachment metadata lost on history reload / session switch / app restart
signals.summary: Chat attachments are rendered from local display text rather than persisted as structured metadata. After a history reload, session switch, or app restart, attachment chips/metadata disappear from the timeline.
signals.review_reason: This is a real user pain point: attachments that users have added to chats disappear after any session change or app restart, making attached files unreliable as a persistent record. The issue has clear acceptance criteria and is a confirmed regression gap from PR #424. While count=1, this is a visible feature loss for any user relying on chat attachments.

source_issues.title: Persist chat attachment metadata across history reloads
source_issues.evidence: Follow-up from PR #424. Chat attachments are rendered from local display text instead of persisted as structured metadata. After history reload, session switch, or app restart, attachment chips disappear. Acceptance criteria: attached files must remain visible after all three scenarios. Bug confirmed by PR author as a known follow-up blocker.

signals.topic: Node auto-approve tests use non-deterministic Task.Delay waits
signals.summary: Auto-approve tests in the node use short Task.Delay() waits for negative assertions (proving something did not happen) and depend on production 1s reconnect delay. This makes tests fragile and non-deterministic.
aliases: flaky auto-approve tests due to timing
signals.review_reason: Non-deterministic tests can cause CI flakiness and silent regressions in the auto-approve feature. While this is labeled as enhancement, it represents a real risk of false-negative test results in a security-sensitive feature (auto-approval of node requests). The author confirms the fragility during review. Keeping as P2 because it is a test-quality concern rather than a direct user-impact bug.

source_issues.title: Make node auto-approve tests deterministic
source_issues.evidence: PR #457 auto-approval tests use short Task.Delay() waits to prove negative cases and depend on production 1s reconnect delay. Author-identified during review. Requires replacing timing-based assertions with deterministic signals and injecting a delay/time provider into GatewayConnectionManager.

signals.topic: Telegram message processing completely blocked by update spool error — all inbound messages stop processing
signals.summary: Three independent issues all describe Telegram channel message processing failures where users receive NO responses at all. The spool blocks, dispatch hangs, or stale .processing claims prevent messages from being handled.
signals.review_reason: Three independent issues (count=3) all describing Telegram message processing failure where users receive NO responses at all. This is main flow blocking — users expect agent responses but nothing happens. High frequency across issues confirms a systemic Telegram channel problem, not an edge case.

source_issues.title: Telegram: Bot not initialized — update spool blocks all message processing
source_issues.evidence: Error 'Bot not initialized' causes drain loop to break, leaving update in spool. ALL subsequent spooled updates stop being processed, blocking all Telegram inbound messages until gateway restart.

source_issues.title: Telegram inbound dispatch hangs after 'Inbound message' log
source_issues.evidence: dispatchTelegramMessage never resolves after logging 'Inbound message'. No model call, no error, no outbound. Second message onwards hangs silently. Webhook shows pending_update_count: 0 (update consumed but no reply).

source_issues.title: Telegram isolated ingress spool can remain blocked by stale .processing claim after gateway recreate
source_issues.evidence: Stale .processing file blocks later Telegram updates. Survived gateway recreate. Messages queued but not processed. Required manual intervention to unblock.

signals.topic: Compaction does not write summary to daily memory — silent regression causing data loss

aliases: Daily memory not written on compaction
signals.review_reason: P1 because it causes data loss — user conversation summaries are silently not saved during compaction. Regression from previously fixed issue confirms this broke existing functionality. While count=1, the severity (data loss) and regression status justify P1.

source_issues.title: openclaw onboard re-run discards existing agents.list and bindings — silent loss of all configured agents
source_issues.evidence: Re-running onboard rewrites config and discards agents.list and bindings arrays. Command reports success. Config collapses from ~9.9KB to ~1.8KB. All configured agents silently orphaned. Failure delayed until gateway restart makes root cause hard to find.

signals.topic: Symlink loop in working directory causes uncaught RuntimeError, crashing aider during repo-map initialization

This uncaught exception crashes aider during the repo-map generation phase, blocking the entire coding workflow for repositories containing these problematic files.

This crashes the core repo-map feature, which is central to aider's workflow. Both issues share identical error messages and stack traces pointing to the same root cause. signals.topic: litellm exception list mismatch causes uncaught ValueError crash at startup
signals.summary: Aider maintains its own exceptions list that must stay in sync with litellm's exceptions. When litellm adds a new exception class (e.g., `BadGatewayError`) that is not yet in aider's list, the `LiteLLMExceptions._load()` method raises an uncaught `ValueError`, crashing aider immediately on startup or first message send.
signals.review_reason: This is a structural sync bug: every time litellm adds an exception class not in aider's hand-maintained list, aider crashes. The crash occurs at core initialization (LiteLLMExceptions._load), blocking all usage. While only 1 report in this window, the root cause is systematic — it will recur with each new litellm release. Confirmed P0 due to complete startup blockage and structural recurrence risk.

source_issues.title: Uncaught ValueError in exceptions.py line 66
source_issues.evidence: ValueError: BadGatewayError is in litellm but not in aider's exceptions list — crashes at base_coder.send_message → LiteLLMExceptions() → _load(). State: closed.

signals.topic: Pydantic version incompatibility (Discriminator import) crashes aider on startup
signals.summary: When users have pydantic >= 2.10 installed, `from pydantic import Discriminator` fails because `Discriminator` was moved to a different location in newer pydantic versions. Aider's litellm dependency chain triggers this import at startup, causing an uncaught `ImportError: cannot import name 'Discriminator' from 'pydantic'`, completely blocking aider from starting.
signals.review_reason: Startup crash caused by pydantic version incompatibility in the litellm import chain. While count=1, the impact is complete startup blockage for any user with a pydantic version mismatch. The crash occurs before any user interaction, making it a critical blocker. P1 because it's environment-specific rather than universal, but it is a genuine crash with clear user impact.

source_issues.title: Uncaught ImportError in openai.py line 74
source_issues.evidence: ImportError: cannot import name 'Discriminator' from 'pydantic' — triggered when litellm imports openai.py at aider startup on Windows with Python 3.10. State: open.

signals.topic: benchmark.py CLI flag mismatch (`--read-model-settings` vs `--model-settings-file`) causes silent failure and wasted compute
signals.summary: The benchmark.py script uses `--read-model-settings` but aider's main CLI and documentation use `--model-settings-file` throughout. When users follow documentation links from benchmark.py's README, they pass `--model-settings-file` which is silently ignored, loading no model settings. For models like Qwen-family AWQ that require `min_p`/`top_p` knobs, this causes the benchmark to hang indefinitely in long-decode loops (24-hour timeout), appearing as a silent hang rather than a clear error.
signals.review_reason: This is a significant UX/correctness defect: a CLI flag name inconsistency leads to silent failure. Users following official documentation end up with no model settings loaded, causing benchmarks to hang for up to 24 hours with no error message. The author explicitly spent hours debugging this. The failure mode (silent hang) makes it particularly costly. While count=1, the severity and effort to hit it justify P1 — the issue is inherently underreported because most users silently work around it or give up.

signals.topic: API eval table endpoint allows unbounded page size causing potential server resource exhaustion
signals.summary: GET /api/eval/:id/table accepts any positive integer for limit without upper bound on non-export requests, allowing oversized page requests to load and serialize large amounts of data in one response.
aliases: eval table page size not capped

source_issues.title: Cap eval table page size for non-export requests
source_issues.evidence: A very large limit can make a normal table request ask the server to load and serialize a large amount of eval result data in one response. Other list-style APIs in the server already bound their page sizes, but the eval table endpoint does not.

signals.topic: Orphaned headless Chrome Helper processes spin at high CPU (85-100%) after agent-browser session ends, consuming multiple CPU cores
signals.summary: agent-browser can leave headless Chrome processes running under a temp profile path after the calling agent/session exits or is interrupted. The orphaned Chrome Helper children spin at ~85-100% CPU each, consuming ~5-6 saturated CPU cores until manually killed. This is a resource leak that drains battery, heats the machine, and makes the system appear busy after work has ended.
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed recurring resource leak (#1113 was closed, #1371 is a new recurrence with a different symptom). The user impact is significant: 5-6 full CPU cores spinning at 85-100% after work is supposed to be done, causing real battery drain and machine heating. The problem persists across gateway restarts and requires manual intervention, making it a persistent operational burden rather than a one-off.

source_issues.title: Orphaned headless Chrome Helpers spin at high CPU under agent-browser-chrome temp profile
source_issues.evidence: Headless Chrome processes remain alive after caller exits/interrupted. Multiple Chrome Helper child processes each using 85-100% CPU. Total load approximately 5-6 saturated CPU cores. Processes must be manually killed; restarting the gateway does not clean them up. Issue references #1113 as a similar but distinct manifestation.

source_issues.title: agent-browser leaves zombie Chrome processes after exiting
source_issues.evidence: Previously closed issue on same root cause: zombie Chrome processes after exiting. Confirmed recurrence in #1371.

signals.topic: CDP commands silently execute in wrong execution context when Chromium DevTools is open, producing incorrect results without errors
signals.summary: When attaching to a Chromium instance via --cdp with Chrome DevTools open on the same tab, agent-browser's Runtime.evaluate, Page.navigate, click etc. operate on a secondary execution context fully disconnected from the page's main world. Commands report success and return coherent-looking values, but the visible tab is unaffected and data is wrong.
signals.review_reason: This is a main-flow runtime failure where core CDP commands silently produce incorrect results without any error signal. The user sees 'success' but the actual outcome is wrong, which breaks automated workflows built on agent-browser. The doctor command also fails to detect it. While count=1, the impact is severe: all of eval, open, snapshot, and click are silently wrong under a common DevTools-open scenario, making the tool fundamentally unreliable in this configuration.

source_issues.title: `--cdp` eval/open silently target a secondary execution context when Chromium DevTools is open on the same target
source_issues.evidence: Commands return coherent-looking values with no error but the visible tab is unaffected. eval returns wrong location.href. open reports success but page doesn't move. snapshot returns a different page than the user sees. agent-browser doctor reports 'pass' despite the problem.

signals.topic: snapshot -s <selector> returns duplicate elements when AX tree contains virtual nodes without backendDOMNodeId
signals.summary: The scoped snapshot command incorrectly promotes AX nodes as top-level roots when virtual intermediate nodes (generic/group) lack backendDOMNodeId, causing elements to appear multiple times in output. Elements under the target selector appear N times, each with different @ref values, breaking automations that depend on accurate element lists.
signals.review_reason: This is a data correctness bug that produces wrong output for a core command. The duplicate elements break automations relying on accurate element lists from snapshot. While count=1 and the trigger condition (specific AX tree shape) may be relatively niche, the symptom is clearly wrong behavior from a user-facing command, not a feature limitation.

source_issues.title: snapshot -s <selector> produces duplicate elements when AX tree contains virtual nodes without backendDOMNodeId
source_issues.evidence: Scoped snapshot algorithm breaks parent-child chain at virtual AX nodes with backendDOMNodeId:None, incorrectly promoting descendants as top-level roots. Elements appear multiple times in output, each with different @ref values. Root cause traced to cli/src/native/snapshot.rs step 5. Observed in Alibaba Cloud Apsara Stack Console, a real production page.

signals.topic: agent-browser install fails with 'sh: playwright: command not found' for Homebrew-installed users, blocking entire tool usage

signals.review_reason: This is a startup/blocking failure for Homebrew users. The tool cannot be used at all after Homebrew installation without manual Chromium setup. While count=1, the open state for 3+ months with 9 comments suggests ongoing user frustration. The blocking nature (zero functionality without manual workaround) elevates it from a trivial bug.

signals.topic: streamText/ToolLoopAgent stream silently hangs when fetch body is cancelled mid-stream; abortSignal does not propagate
signals.summary: When a streaming streamText/ToolLoopAgent.stream() call is aborted after response headers arrive but while the body is still streaming (e.g., mid adaptive-thinking + tool calls), streamResult.text and streamResult.steps never resolve or reject — they hang indefinitely. The passed abortSignal fires but does not unstick the promises. No error chunk, no finish chunk is emitted. A 30-minute headless agent run hung silently with no error log, requiring an external watchdog to recover.
signals.review_reason: This is a main flow blocking issue where streaming promises hang forever with no error rejection when the underlying fetch body is cancelled mid-stream. The abortSignal fires but does not propagate to unstick promises. User's agent runs become unrecoverable and require external watchdogs. Affects long-running agentic workflows (10+ minute responses with adaptive thinking + tool calls) where mid-stream abort is the common case, not the exception. Explicit user impact: production 30-minute silent hang with no error log.

source_issues.title: streamText / ToolLoopAgent.stream() silently hangs when fetch body is cancelled mid-stream; abortSignal does not propagate
source_issues.evidence: Main flow blocking: promises hang forever with no error rejection when fetch is aborted mid-stream. 30-minute headless agent run hung silently with no error log. Requires external watchdog. onStepFinish never fires, result.text and result.steps stay pending forever. Affects long-running agentic workflows with adaptive thinking where mid-stream abort is the common case.

signals.topic: GoogleAuth cache reference equality bug causes ~120ms overhead per call and ~6s cold start without GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT env var
signals.summary: The GoogleAuth cache key uses reference equality, but callers pass a fresh {} every time when options are omitted, so the cache never hits. Every call re-instantiates GoogleAuth and re-mints access tokens (~120ms overhead per call). Additionally, createVertex({project, location}) does not propagate project into GoogleAuth, causing a ~3s gcloud subprocess on cold start when GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT is unset.
signals.review_reason: Significant cost loss and UX degradation: every generateText/streamText call re-authenticates unnecessarily, adding ~120ms overhead. Cold starts add ~6s when GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT is unset. Affects all Google Vertex users who don't explicitly pass googleAuthOptions, which is the common case. Documented performance regression with specific measurements.

source_issues.title: [Provider:GoogleVertex] generateAuthToken always misses its GoogleAuth cache (and projectId discovery shells out to gcloud)
source_issues.evidence: Cache never hits for the common no-options case. Cold first call ~6s+ (~3s gcloud subprocess + ~3s auth setup). Every subsequent call ~120ms extra from re-minting tokens. Production impact: 10-50ms overhead per call even on GCP. Measured improvement with workaround: cold 6s→1.1s, warm 500ms→330ms.

Users must fall back to parsing result.text manually.
signals.review_reason: Key feature (structured output) is completely broken when using Cerebras provider with tools. Users get NoOutputGeneratedError and must fall back to manual text parsing, defeating the purpose of structured output. Explicit error with stack trace and workaround documented.

signals.topic: App Router cold start: instrumentation.ts register() races with route handlers, breaking OTel/Sentry/DB pool initialization
signals.summary: RouteModule.prepare does not await ensureInstrumentationRegistered on Vercel cold lambdas. Route handlers begin executing before instrumentation.ts#register() resolves, leaving module-scoped state (OTel patches, DB pools, config globals) as null/undefined on first request. This directly violates the documented guarantee that instrumentation code runs before any other code. Affects all users deploying instrumentation hooks to Vercel serverless with Next.js 16.x.
signals.review_reason: App Router route handlers race with instrumentation.ts#register() on Vercel cold start. This directly breaks critical infrastructure hooks (OTel, Sentry, DB pools) on first request for every user deploying to Vercel serverless with Next.js 16.x. Three independent reports confirm the same root cause. Count=3, affects core observability and data layer initialization — this is a main flow failure for production deployments.

signals.topic: Turbopack build: silent incomplete RSC payload during ISR SSG prerender, producing permanently broken cached HTML
signals.summary: Under Turbopack (Next.js 16 default for build), pages using generateStaticParams + revalidate produce incomplete RSC payloads at build time. The HTML is written to cache with unresolved $L Suspense placeholders. Users see empty pages/hydration skeletons with 'Error: Connection closed' in DevTools. The broken payload is locked into Vercel ISR cache (x-vercel-cache: HIT) with no build warnings. Triggered by specific page complexity/content interactions. Caused a 21-hour production outage affecting 5 pages on maisondetalents.com. Local build/start does NOT reproduce — production-only.
signals.review_reason: Two independent reports document Turbopack silently producing broken ISR cache entries during SSG prerender. Affected pages render as permanent hydration skeletons for end users, locked into Vercel's edge cache. This caused a 21-hour production outage on a live e-commerce site with 5 pages down. The failure is silent at build time (no warnings, exit code 0) — the first signal is user complaints. The worst possible failure mode for ISR.

source_issues.title: [Bug] Next.js 16 + turbopack + ISR: silent incomplete RSC payload on SSG prerender (generateStaticParams + revalidate, production-only)
source_issues.evidence: 21-hour outage on maisondetalents.com on 2026-05-16. 5 pages (/, /brands, /brands/[slug], /guide/interview/[brand], /guide/store/[slug]) affected. Broken pages: HTTP 200, x-vercel-cache: HIT, x-nextjs-prerender: 1, but HTML body contains $L10-$L30+ placeholders. curl shows ~184KB partial RSC payload. Users see empty pages.

signals.summary: After upgrading to Next.js 16.2.6, navigating back via the browser back button causes all client-side JavaScript to stop executing on the restored page. No errors, warnings, or stack traces are logged. The page visually restores but all interactions become unresponsive. Affects both Chrome and Edge consistently on Windows. Regression — works on 16.2.3 and below.
signals.review_reason: Browser back navigation completely disables JavaScript on the restored page in Next.js 16.2.6 — a confirmed regression from 16.2.3. Back navigation is a fundamental browser interaction used constantly during development and end-user browsing. No error logging makes this nearly impossible to debug without knowing the cause. This blocks the most common navigation pattern for every affected user.

signals.topic: history.pushState URL silently reverts when page has prefetched Link + middleware cookie redirect
signals.summary: Calling history.pushState to change a URL parameter silently reverts to the previous URL within ~1 frame when: (1) the page contains a <Link> whose href matches the original URL state (causing Next.js prefetch cache to cache the original URL entry), (2) a useEffect writes URL state to a cookie, and (3) middleware redirects based on the cookie. The combination causes Next.js router to 'restore' the old prefetch entry, undoing the pushState. Users see the URL flash then revert, breaking filter/sort/dashboard UIs.
signals.review_reason: history.pushState silently reverts URLs in a common pattern combining prefetched Links and middleware cookie redirects. This breaks filter, sort, and parameter-based UIs — a core navigation pattern in Next.js apps. The reversion is silent (no error thrown), making it a confusing UX where user actions appear to have no effect. Production-impacting for any app using URL state with middleware.

source_issues.title: Bug: history.pushState to a new URL reverts when route has a prefetched Link + proxy.ts cookie-based redirect
source_issues.evidence: URL flashes to new value then reverts within ~1 frame. RSC tree stays for old URL. Root cause: Next.js monkey-patches pushState and the prefetch cache lookup fuzzy-matches the old prefetched entry. Breaks any dashboard/filter UI using pushState with middleware cookie redirects.

signals.topic: turbo prune generates invalid pnpm lockfile with peer-variant injected workspace deps, causing pnpm install --frozen-lockfile to crash
signals.summary: turbo prune --docker drops the base packages entry for peer-variant injected workspace deps in the pruned pnpm-lock.yaml. The base entry holding the `directory` resolution is silently dropped, leaving pnpm with `resolution: undefined`, causing `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` to crash with 'Cannot use in operator to search for directory in undefined'. This breaks Docker multi-stage builds that rely on turbo prune.
aliases: turbo prune pnpm peer-variant injected workspace deps crash
signals.review_reason: turbo prune producing a lockfile that causes the package manager to crash mid-Docker-build is a main-flow failure. The bug is isolated to turbo prune by the reporter (original lockfile works, pruned one crashes), and the crash prevents the Docker image build from completing. Affects core CI/CD workflow.

source_issues.title: turbo prune drops the base packages entry for peer-variant injected workspace deps, breaking pnpm install
source_issues.evidence: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile crashes with 'Cannot use in operator to search for directory in undefined' when using the pruned pnpm-lock.yaml. Original lockfile works, only pruned output crashes. Repro with two apps pinning different react versions + injectWorkspacePackages + dependenciesMeta.injected.

signals.topic: turbo prune --docker emits invalid Bun lockfile, causing bun install --frozen-lockfile to fail
signals.summary: turbo prune --docker generates an out/json/bun.lock that Bun considers stale. Running bun install --frozen-lockfile inside the pruned directory fails because Bun detects unexpected changes in the lockfile. This blocks Docker builds that rely on turbo prune for Bun workspaces.
aliases: turbo prune bun lockfile stale frozen-lockfile fails
bun install --frozen-lockfile fails on pruned output
signals.review_reason: turbo prune emitting a lockfile that fails the frozen-lockfile check is a main-flow CI/CD failure. Docker builds relying on turbo prune for Bun workspaces are blocked. Issue is confirmed with a minimal reproducible example.

source_issues.title: turbo prune --docker emits Bun lockfile that fails bun install --frozen-lockfile
source_issues.evidence: bun install --frozen-lockfile fails in out/json with 'lockfile had changes, but lockfile is frozen'. Minimal repro with two apps (api with sequelize-cli, front with eslint-config-next) shows turbo prune produces a stale bun.lock. Closed as bug.

signals.topic: Turbo installation fails on Windows due to missing binary detection, turbo.exe not found
signals.summary: Installing turbo via npm on Windows fails to locate the correct platform binary. Despite turbo-windows-64 being present in node_modules, turbo looks for the binary at turbo-windows-64/bin/turbo.exe and fails, falling back to finding linux binaries instead. The tool is completely unusable on Windows from a fresh install.
aliases: Windows binary not found npm install turbo
turbo-windows-64 binary not found postinstall script
signals.review_reason: A fresh npm install that renders the entire tool unusable is a critical user-facing failure. This is not an edge case - it affects any Windows user attempting to use turbo, including in CI environments. The tool cannot be run at all after installation.

source_issues.title: Turborepo Installation Fails on Windows - Missing Binaries
source_issues.evidence: Fresh npm install of turbo on Windows 11 produces missing binary errors. turbo reports 'did not find the correct binary for your platform (windows 64)' and lists the wrong paths. Identical setup works in WSL2. Blocks all turbo usage on Windows from first install.

signals.topic: Graceful shutdown does not work on Windows, tasks killed immediately on Ctrl+C
signals.summary: On Windows (PowerShell and CMD), turbo does not perform graceful shutdown when the user presses Ctrl+C. All child tasks are killed immediately instead of being given the opportunity to shut down cleanly. This is a platform-specific regression where Linux/WSL behavior (tasks shut down gracefully) does not apply to Windows, leading to data loss or incomplete state for long-running dev tasks.
aliases: Windows graceful shutdown fails ctrl+c kills tasks immediately
turbo start graceful shutdown Windows broken
signals.review_reason: Graceful shutdown failing on Windows causes child processes to be abruptly killed, risking data loss in long-running tasks (dev servers, watch modes). This is a platform-specific regression that makes the development experience on Windows significantly worse than on Linux/WSL.

source_issues.title: Graceful shutdown does not work on Windows (PowerShell / CMD)
source_issues.evidence: On Linux/WSL, Ctrl+C triggers graceful shutdown showing 'Graceful shutdown start/end' and tasks complete in ~6s. On Windows PowerShell, tasks are killed immediately (~1s) without graceful shutdown. Affects all long-running tasks started with turbo (e.g. dev servers, watch modes).

signals.topic: Turbo causes 100% CPU usage and system freeze when building large monorepos
signals.summary: When building a monorepo with 43 packages, turbo consumes 100% CPU and renders the entire computer unresponsive. The same build with pnpm -r build completes normally with expected CPU usage. Additionally, a brief popup window appears for each package being built, which does not occur with pnpm -r build.
aliases: turbo extremely slow 100% CPU blocking computer
signals.review_reason: 100% CPU usage causing system-wide freezes represents a significant degradation of user experience. While only one reporter is documented here, such extreme resource consumption affecting multi-package monorepos is a notable performance pain point. Classified as P2 due to count=1 and the issue being closed (though recently active).

source_issues.title: Extremely slow with 100% CPU usage
source_issues.evidence: Building 43-package monorepo with turbo causes 100% CPU and system freeze. Same build with pnpm -r build completes normally. Reporter attached a profiler profile. No equivalent issue with pnpm -r build for the same packages.

signals.topic: CLI 54.x regression causing production build failures across Vite-based frameworks (Vite SPA dev-code-in-bundle + SvelteKit route resolution broken)
signals.summary: Vercel CLI 54.x introduced regressions that silently corrupt production build outputs for Vite-based frameworks. In Vite SPAs, the pre-build `vite.resolveConfig()` call pollutes `process.env.NODE_ENV`, causing production bundles to embed `import.meta.env.DEV=true` and expose development-only code to real users. In SvelteKit apps, `/admin/*` routes return 404 despite correct build artifacts. Both issues reproduce on CLI 54.x and are absent on CLI 53.x.
signals.review_reason: Two separate but closely related production-breaking regressions introduced in CLI 54.x. Issue #16380 causes development-only code to be silently embedded in production Vite bundles (real users see dev UI), which is a critical and silent production failure. Issue #16377 causes SvelteKit admin routes to return 404 in production, blocking the main workflow for affected apps. Both are silent regressions absent in CLI 53.x, meaning existing deployments silently broke after upgrade. P0 despite count=2 because production is directly blocked (dev code exposure and broken routing both affect live user-facing apps), and both have clear reproduction steps and downgrade workarounds.

source_issues.title: [@vercel/static-build@2.9.28、CLI 54.2.0] Production Vite build produces import.meta.env.DEV=true after vite.resolveConfig pre-scan
source_issues.evidence: Production bundle contains DEV:true PROD:false with MODE:production — development-only UI/debug text shipped to real users. Silent regression (no error thrown). Only reproducible on CLI 54.x vs 53.x on same commit.

source_issues.title: CLI 54.2.0 breaks SvelteKit route resolution for /admin/* routes
source_issues.evidence: /admin/* routes (18+ sub-routes) render 404 error page in production with CLI 54.2.0. Server responds 200 + x-sveltekit-page:true — SvelteKit runs but route matching fails. Same code works on CLI 53.3.2. Blocks core admin functionality in production.

signals.topic: @vercel/next@4.17.1 build error — Unable to find lambda for route with Next.js 16 static-PPR routes (chain.headers)
signals.summary: When using Next.js 16 with PPR-enabled cache components, builds fail with 'Unable to find lambda for route' because the lambda key remap is bypassed when Next.js 16 populates the new routesManifest.ppr.chain.headers field.
aliases: Unable to find lambda for route PARTIALLY_STATIC
signals.review_reason: Build failure that blocks Next.js 16 PPR deployment. The error is explicit and prevents the main deployment flow. However, count=1 and it's a specific edge case tied to a very new Next.js 16 feature, so P2. Root cause is well-identified and reproducible.

source_issues.title: @vercel/next@4.17.1: static-PPR routes fail lambda lookup when Next.js 16 chain.headers is enabled
source_issues.evidence: Build throws 'Error: Unable to find lambda for route: /foo' — blocks deployment entirely for Next.js 16 apps using 'use cache' with cacheTag/cacheLife. Root cause is clearly identified: lambda stored under /foo/page key but lookup uses /foo when chain.headers is defined.

signals.topic: vercel ls displays 'UNKNOWN' status for blocked/cancelled deployments instead of readable label
signals.summary: When deployments are blocked or cancelled, `vercel ls` shows 'UNKNOWN' in the Status column instead of a human-readable 'BLOCKED' or 'CANCELLED' label, causing confusion about actual deployment state.
signals.review_reason: UX degradation — the CLI status output is misleading and causes user confusion. Deployment itself is not blocked but users cannot interpret their deployment state. Low impact but real user experience issue with clear fix path.

source_issues.title: vercel ls shows UNKNOWN status for BLOCKED deployments
source_issues.evidence: API returns readyState='BLOCKED' but CLI does not map this value to a readable label, displaying 'UNKNOWN' instead. Deployment status column is uninterpretable for blocked deployments.

signals.topic: vercel env add preview --yes non-interactive mode fails with git_branch_required, blocking CI/CD automation

aliases: vercel env add preview automation broken
signals.review_reason: CLI usability bug that blocks automation/CI use cases. The CLI self-contradicts by suggesting a command form that it then rejects. Real workflow impact for automated deployments, but single occurrence and non-blocking for interactive human use.

source_issues.title: vercel env add NAME preview --value <V> --yes returns git_branch_required despite hint suggesting that exact form
source_issues.evidence: CLI's own error message suggests using the exact command that was just rejected. Non-interactive CI/CD pipeline is broken for adding preview env vars. Interactive mode works; only --yes path fails.
